review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the sl2M, conjAdj_apply and bridge-lemma uses. I did not read the p2m_export or p2m_reactivate macros, so I don't know what they do to simp sets or visibility. I have not run Lean. The findings are about missing simp lemmas and rewrite-bridging, not about observed simp failures. I found no simp-loop risk. The one scoped simp lemma, conjAdj_apply, unfolds a definition to a normal form that matches endToMatrix_twAd, so I did not flag it.

findings.excerpt: private def _root_.WCOTGlueBCore.sl2M (s t u : R) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R := Matrix.of ![![s, t], ![u, -s]]
findings.problem: sl2M is the main matrix family in the file. It has no simp lemmas: no entry lemmas, no scalar-multiple lemma and no square-zero or product lemma. Every proof therefore unfolds it with `simp [sl2M]` after a case split on entries (`ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [sl2M, ...]`). The same inline facts are reproved many times. `sl2M 0 t 0 = t • sl2M 0 1 0` is proved as `hE` and `hsE` in conjAdj_sl2M_eq. It is proved again as `sl2M_smul_eq`, which sits much later (line 763), so earlier proofs cannot use it. `sl2M 0 t 0 * sl2M 0 t 0 = 0` is reproved as `hE2` at least twice. Proofs depend on unfolding the definition instead of on a stable simp normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Next to the definition, add simp lemmas such as `sl2M_apply_zero_zero`, `sl2M_apply_zero_one`, `sl2M_apply_one_zero` and `sl2M_apply_one_one` (entries `s`, `t`, `u`, `-s`), and a `sl2M_mul_sl2M` lemma. Move `sl2M_smul_eq` up beside the definition, in the direction `sl2M 0 b 0 = b • sl2M 0 1 0` or its reverse, whichever the callers need. Prove `hE` and `hsE` in conjAdj_sl2M_eq and `hE2` (lines 600 and 835) from these lemmas. The `fin_cases ... simp [sl2M]` calls can then mostly become plain `simp`.
findings.benefit: The entries of `sl2M` simplify in one canonical way, and repeated one-off identities get a single named lemma. Proofs stop depending on how `sl2M` is defined, which also helps with the duplicated copies of the definition.

theorem sl2M_smul_eq {R : Type} [CommRing R] (b : R) : sl2M (0 : R) b 0 = b • sl2M 0 1 0 := by
have hE2 : sl2M (0 : 𝒪) 1 0 * sl2M 0 1 0 = 0 := by

findings.declaration: WCOTGlueBFinal.sl2M_B6_eq / sl2M_adapt_eq (bridges between duplicate sl2M definitions)
findings.excerpt: theorem sl2M_B6_eq (s t u : R) : WCOTDevB6.sl2M s t u = sl2M s t u := rfl
findings.problem: The file defines `sl2M` three times with the same body, as private defs in WCOTGlueBCore, WCOTDevB6 and WCOTGlueBAdapt. The two bridge lemmas are `rfl` equations that are not simp lemmas and are not applied by simp. Callers must use manual `rw [sl2M_B6_eq]`, `rw [← sl2M_B6_eq, ← key, hT1]` and `rw [WCOTGlueBFinal.sl2M_adapt_eq] at hconj`, and must keep track of which copy a term uses. `simp [sl2M]` unfolds only the copy that is in scope. Facts about one copy, such as the `simp [sl2M]` entry computations, do not transfer to the others. The `←` rewrites also run in the direction that reintroduces the duplicate copy. Terms are therefore not kept in one normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `WCOTDevB6.sl2M` and `WCOTGlueBAdapt.sl2M`. Reuse the single `WCOTGlueBCore.sl2M`, either by opening it or by moving the lemmas that use the copies, `eq_line_of_unipotent_mul` and `exists_conj_eq_sl2M`, into that namespace. This makes `sl2M_B6_eq`, `sl2M_adapt_eq` and the `rw` calls at lines 594, 597, 646, 809, 824 and 828 unnecessary. If the copies must stay, mark the bridge lemmas `@[simp]` oriented toward `WCOTGlueBCore.sl2M`. They are `rfl` and fit that orientation, and they would cause no loop.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical `sl2M`, so the simp lemmas proposed in the first finding apply everywhere. The manual conversions between copies disappear.
